title: SXSW Reveals First 100 Artists for 2027 Music Festival
summary: Acts from 21 countries make the opening wave, with Billboard, NPR Music, KCRW and BBC Introducing among the first showcase presenters.
contentText:
SXSW has announced the first 100 showcasing artists for its 2027 Music Festival & Conference, running March 15-21 in Austin. The opening wave draws acts from 21 countries, selected from thousands of submissions.

Named in the first round are Rome Streetz, the Griselda Records signee known for hardcore hip-hop; Wild Pink, the indie rock act known for heartland songwriting; New Orleans rapper La Reezy; and LYNN, the Birmingham-born, Austin-based rapper coming off a viral On The Radar freestyle.

The international contingent includes ANASOF in contemporary Latin songwriting; Japanese live band bed, blending techno, punk and pop; Boko Yout, whose alt-rock experimentation has made them one of Europe’s most-discussed new acts; Scottish punk duo Cowboy Hunters; Irish-Cornish quintet Girl in the Year Above, pairing Celtic storytelling with alt-rock; and La Fiera de Ojinaga , the Mexican regional act working traditional Norteño music with a distinctive Norteño Sax sound.

“These first 100 artists, curated by our team from thousands of submissions, represent the quality and diversity attendees can expect when the global music industry gathers at SXSW,” said Brian Hobbs, vp of music at SXSW, citing record attendance across seven nights of showcases in 2026. “More than ever, SXSW is the place where artists break and the business of music gets done.”

SXSW also named its first showcase presenters for 2027: BBC Introducing, Bella Union, Billboard, British Music Embassy, De Los of LA Times, KCRW, Luck Reunion, Monster Children, NPR Music, Rolling Stone, SoundOn TikTok and United Masters. Showcases are curated by SXSW programmers with labels, agencies, export offices, management and PR firms, publishers, media outlets, brands and festivals.

The music conference programming, announced last month as part of more than 350 sessions across SXSW’s Innovation, Film & TV and Music tracks, centers on four themes: financial sustainability, touring, community building and technology. Sessions include “Can Brands Save Live Music?” with speakers from Visa, Superfly and Imagination; “How Women Fans and Artists Are Redefining Fandom,” built around a 15,000-respondent study on women’s role in driving ticket volume and premium spending; and “AI After the Hype: What Artists Actually Use,” with speakers from Splice and Image Line.

The festival footprint moves closer to the action in 2027. The Music Clubhouse relocates to The Thompson hotel, with conference programming split between The Thompson and The Westin — off Sixth Street and three blocks from the Red River Cultural District.

Applications for music showcases close Friday (Nov. 20) at 11:59 p.m. Badges and wristbands are on sale now.
